artist_scope: full contract (Tier 2, the state-branching class (an attacking branch on the jaw and tail): geckolib_migration_design.md section 5); the rig is not yet in-game (it lands through the seam in a later slice)
character_sheet: A big sprawling lizard with a sail: three body blocks, a neck carrying an upper jaw with three nose pieces, two angled eyes, two crest ('hat') pieces and eleven upper teeth, a hinged lower jaw with six teeth, four two-part legs with feet and two toes each, a five-segment tail, and along the back a fan of eight fin pieces with seven ridge spines (LizardModel.java createBodyLayer; 71 parts on a 128x128 sheet). It is a hunter rather than a monster: 30 HP, 6 damage (Lizard.java:95-100) - every tenth think tick it looks 12 blocks around for attack squids, spiders, cave spiders and chickens (:134-146, :155-159) and bites within 3.5 blocks (:223-227, doHurtTarget :116-118), raising a synched attacking flag while prey is close (:224, cleared :235). A cod makes it your buddy for 3000-5000 ticks (:121-132); it wanders a lot (:83), floats (:79), seeks water when dry (:202-215), heals slowly (:217), shrugs off cactus (:107), breeds on cod (:81, :261) and has a half-size baby (LizardRenderer.java:41-42). It spawns above y 50 (:272-274). Read it as a monitor lizard: a splayed, wiggling stride, a lazy tail that turns into a lash when prey is close, a jaw that chomps.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig, x0.5 as a baby (LizardRenderer.java:26, 41-42) on a 128x128 sheet (LizardModel.java:527); the hitbox is 1.5 x 1.25 (ModEntities.java:550-552); shadow 0.75 (LizardRenderer.java:28).

groups.name: gait
groups.axis: y (upper legs, feet, toes) / x (lower legs)
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the walking speed at 1.0 x 0.65, no rest offsets - still below the 0.1 threshold
groups.plain: the splayed stride: both front upper legs, feet and toes yaw one way and both back ones the other, while the lower legs pitch in diagonal pairs (front left with back right)
groups.math: a = limbSwingAmount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 1.0 * 0.65) * pi * 0.25 * limbSwingAmount : 0; TopFront*Leg / Front*Foot / Toe1,2,3,8 .yRot = a; TopBack*Leg / Back*Foot / Toe4-7 .yRot = -a; BottomFrontLeftLeg.xRot = a; BottomFrontRightLeg.xRot = -a; BottomBackLeftLeg.xRot = -a; BottomBackRightLeg.xRot = a
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.0 x 0.65 (wingspeed, LizardModel.java:21): the natural period is 2 pi / 0.65 = 9.7 ticks

groups.name: jaw
groups.amplitude: calm: held at 0.25 rad (14 deg open), no motion; attacking: 0.52 rad rest then 0.35 rad (20 deg) either way at 0.45 (no wingspeed on this term)
groups.plain: the lower jaw and its six teeth hang slightly open at rest and chomp wide when prey is close
groups.phase: the attacking flag selects the branch (Lizard.java:224, :235)
groups.omega_note: the phase is ageInTicks x 0.45 (no wingspeed): the natural period is 2 pi / 0.45 = 14 ticks

groups.name: tail
groups.amplitude: calm: pi x 0.05 = 0.157 rad at 0.25 x 0.65, taken x 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0 / 1.25 along the chain (2 to 11 deg); attacking: pi x 0.35 = 1.1 rad at 1.25 x 0.65 (omega 0.8125), the same multipliers (16 to 79 deg at the tip)
groups.plain: a lazy side-to-side sway of the whole tail, each segment swinging wider than the one before; when prey is close it becomes a fast, wide lash
groups.math: n = attacking ? cos(t * 1.25 * 0.65) * pi * 0.35 : cos(t * 0.25 * 0.65) * pi * 0.05; TailBase1.yRot = n * 0.25; Tail2.yRot = n * 0.5; Tail3.yRot = n * 0.75; Tail4.yRot = n * 1.0; TailTip.yRot = n * 1.25; each segment's x/z placed along the previous segment's yaw (12, 9, 7, 7 units)
groups.phase: the attacking flag selects the rhythm (Lizard.java:224, :235)
groups.omega_note: the calm phase is ageInTicks x 0.25 x 0.65: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.1625 = 38.7 ticks; attacking 2 pi / 0.8125 = 7.7 ticks

behaviour: One gait rhythm on the legs (LizardModel.java:533-553): above a walking speed of 0.1 the cosine of the age x 1.0 x 0.65 (wingspeed, :21), x pi x 0.25, x the walking speed (45 degrees at full stride every 9.7 ticks) YAWS the upper legs, feet and toes - both front legs one way, both back legs the other, a sprawling wiggle - and PITCHES the lower legs in diagonal pairs (front left and back right forward while front right and back left go back). Below the threshold the legs snap to their rests.

The lower jaw and its six teeth (LizardModel.java:554-560) hold 0.25 rad (14 deg) open when calm and chomp when the attacking flag is up: 0.52 rad plus the cosine of the age x 0.45 (no wingspeed) x 0.35 - 20 degrees either way around a 30-degree gape every 14 ticks.

The five-segment tail sways (LizardModel.java:561-577): calm, the cosine of the age x 0.25 x 0.65 x pi x 0.05, attacking the cosine of the age x 1.25 x 0.65 x pi x 0.35 - each segment takes 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 and 1.25 of it, so the tip swings five times as far as the base (11 degrees calm, 79 attacking), and each next segment's position is re-derived along the previous segment's yaw (12, 9, 7, 7 units): an FK chain written by hand on flat bones - when the rig lands a keyframed sway must key the positions too, or the tail must be parented.

The head follows the look yaw with no pitch (LizardModel.java:578-659): the neck takes a quarter of netHeadYaw; the upper jaw and everything on it - the five nose pieces, the two eyes (with +-0.78 rad offsets), ten upper teeth and the two crest pieces - take half of it, placed 2 units along the neck's yaw; the lower jaw and its teeth take the same half yaw placed 3 units along. Twenty-eight parts are moved by copying the jaw's position and yaw one by one.

The three body blocks, the eight sail fins and the seven ridge spines never move; the attacking flag is held server-side while prey is within 3.5 blocks (Lizard.java:223-224) and cleared when no prey is found (:235), so it is a state, not a pulse.
The renderer halves the scale for a baby (LizardRenderer.java:41-42); water and buddy-following are navigation, not pose (Lizard.java:202-215, :239-241).
